updates.title: Tech View and Board View are unavailable while Imported is selected
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.

Imported work order {Work-order-1} (for example ZZIMP-154648-1) exists at {Location-A} for customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST C154648 Imported"); it came from an invoice import, so it is listed only when Imported is ticked in Status.
Ordinary work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17581) for {Customer-A} exists at {Location-A}.
On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in the Status filter.
steps: Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
Click List in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar.
Click Status and tick "Imported".
Hover the Tech View button in the display switcher and read its tooltip.
Click the Tech View button.
Hover the Board View button in the display switcher and read its tooltip.
Click the Board View button.
Click Status and click "Clear selection".
Click Tech View in the display switcher.
Click Status.
Hover the "Imported" option and read its tooltip.
Try to tick "Imported".
Click Board View in the display switcher.
Click Status.
Hover the "Imported" option and read its tooltip.
Try to tick "Imported".
results: Step 3: the List shows the Imported work orders, including {Work-order-1}.
Steps 4 and 6: the Tech View and Board View buttons are greyed out. Hovering each shows the tooltip "Not available while Imported is selected."
Steps 5 and 7: neither button opens its display. The page stays on List and keeps showing {Work-order-1}.
Step 9: with Imported no longer selected, Tech View opens.
Steps 11 and 12: in Tech View the "Imported" option in Status is greyed out with the tooltip "Imported work orders open in List." It cannot be ticked.
Steps 15 and 16: in Board View the "Imported" option in Status is greyed out with the same tooltip, "Imported work orders open in List." It cannot be ticked.
updates.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 48 (12 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R1, S1-R13a and S1-R13b (added in version 48) with their context note (engineering proposal 17 Sep 2026, agreed by Sasha Grosman 24 Sep 2026, confirmed by Chris Ward 12 Oct 2026), read 14 Oct 2026. Secondary: Work Orders Board View & Tech View Display Options Technical Implementation Plan (revised 24 Sep 2026, uploaded 8 Oct 2026), section 1.4 (follow-up A3) and section 3.26. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026).
quotes: S1-R13a

Imported work orders open in List only. While "Imported" is selected in the Status filter in List, the Board View and Tech View options are greyed out with the tooltip "Not available while Imported is selected."
S1-R1
The Work Orders toolbar offers List, Tech View, and Board View display options.
S1-R13b
In Board View and Tech View, "Imported" is greyed out in the Status filter with the tooltip "Imported work orders open in List."
Tech plan 3.26 Imported

Imported is excluded from the board displays (follow-up A3). While the Imported status chip is selected, Tech View and Board View are disabled in the switcher with a tooltip; while in Tech View or Board View, the Imported option in the Status filter is disabled.
doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on.

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, with no display switcher).

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST C154648 Imported") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Create the Imported work order from an invoice import: your initials > Settings > Invoices (in the IMPORTS group; on some builds Settings > Data Import > Invoices) > Download Template. Fill one row and keep the heading row (the columns marked * are required): Shop Location = the name of {Location-A}, Customer = the name of {Customer-A}, Invoice Number (for example ZZIMP-154648-1), Invoice Date as month/day/year (for example 10/14/2026), Item Labor, a Line Title (for example ZZAUTOTEST labor), Qty 1, Rate 100, Total 100, Tax Amount 5.

Save the file as .csv, click Select CSV File, pick the file and click Import Invoices. The message reads "All invoices have been imported successfully." The imported work order's number is the Invoice Number you typed. This is {Work-order-1}.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Add Line. In the next New Line form type "clutch", pick "Service - Adjust clutch", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17581). This is {Work-order-2}.
Go to Work Orders > All > List, click Status and, if anything is ticked, click "Clear selection".

Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > List: with Status > "Imported" ticked, {Work-order-1} is listed. With the selection cleared, {Work-order-2} is listed and {Work-order-1} is not. Leave nothing ticked in Status. If no Imported work order can be made, the case cannot start: mark it Blocked and write why.
doc_part2: Goal: an Imported work order {Work-order-1} and an ordinary work order {Work-order-2} at {Location-A}, then the case's steps on screen.

Create {Customer-A}, then the import file as in Part 1. UNVERIFIED on the Work Orders QA site: whether the import also creates a customer that does not exist yet; create {Customer-A} first so it does not matter.
Record {Work-order-1} (the Invoice Number) and {Work-order-2} (the number on its page). Check in List with Status > Imported ticked that {Work-order-1} is listed, then clear the selection.

Steps 4 and 6: hover each display button with Playwright and read the tooltip text exactly; compare it character for character with "Not available while Imported is selected." Steps 5 and 7: click each button and confirm the address and the table did not change.
Steps 11 and 15: open Status, hover the Imported option and read its tooltip exactly ("Imported work orders open in List."); steps 12 and 16: click it and confirm it did not become ticked.

UNVERIFIED: the design export of 14 Oct shows Imported work orders inside Tech View and Board View's Unassigned with a lock and no greyed switcher; the PRD (version 48) wins. A build that still behaves like the design fails this case.
Evidence: a screenshot after each step that has an expected result, the build marker, and the real value of every brace name.
updates.change_summary: Rewritten in full to the 8 Oct layout; expects the exact tooltips "Not available while Imported is selected." and "Imported work orders open in List." (S1-R13a/S1-R13b, PRD v48), quotes the PRD instead of only the tech plan; steps split one action per line with tooltip reads; placeholders {Work-order-1}/{Work-order-2}/{Customer-A}; setup moved to the doc.

updates.title: The clear-shifts question appears only for the old lead's unfinished shifts
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-C} (for example Dana Ortiz) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Only Unfinished") is used by this case only.

Six Approved work orders for {Customer-A}, {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-6} (for example S10043-17581 to S10043-17586), are led by {Technician-A}, and each has two approved lines (for example "Service - Full grease service" and "Service - Adjust clutch").
On {Work-order-3} the two lines are {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
Approved work order {Work-order-7} (for example S10043-17587) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-B}.
Work order {Work-order-1} has a shift for {Technician-A} tomorrow 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order.
Work order {Work-order-2} has no shifts at all.
Work order {Work-order-3} has a shift for {Technician-A} tomorrow 8:00–12:00 on {Line-1} only, not on {Line-2}.
Work order {Work-order-4} has a shift for {Technician-A} covering the entire work order that has already ended (for example yesterday 8:00–12:00).
Work order {Work-order-5} has a shift for {Technician-C} tomorrow 8:00–12:00 covering the entire work order, and none for {Technician-A}.
Work order {Work-order-6} has no shifts, while {Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 13:00–15:00 covering the entire work order {Work-order-7}.
No other shift is booked on {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-6}.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
Read the title of the question that opens.
Click Keep shifts.
Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column and note whether a question opens (if one does, click Keep shifts).
Drag {Work-order-3} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column and note whether a question opens (if one does, click Keep shifts).
Drag {Work-order-4} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column and note whether a question opens (if one does, click Keep shifts).
Drag {Work-order-5} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column and note whether a question opens (if one does, click Keep shifts).
Drag {Work-order-6} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column and note whether a question opens (if one does, click Keep shifts).
results: Step 4: dragging {Work-order-1} opens the question "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?").

Steps 6 to 10: {Work-order-2} (no shift), {Work-order-3} (a shift on {Line-1} only, not on every line), {Work-order-4} (only an ended shift), {Work-order-5} (only {Technician-C}'s shift) and {Work-order-6} ({Technician-A}'s shift is on another work order) each move to {Technician-B}'s column straight away with the message "Lead technician updated" and no question.
Steps 3 to 10: the question opened for 1 of the 6 work orders ({Work-order-1}) and for none of the other 5.
updates.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 48 (12 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R28 (reworded in version 47 on 12 Oct 2026 after SV-11126: a work-order-level shift is one that covers every current line), S4-R29 and S4-R5, read 14 Oct 2026. PO answer to engineering, Sasha Grosman 24 Sep 2026 (only the outgoing lead's whole-work-order shifts that have not ended), as recorded in the Technical Implementation Plan section 1.4. Every work order has two lines because the Schedule books a one-line work order at once as a whole, and whether a shift on the only line of a one-line work order counts is an open question to the PO (14 Oct 2026). Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026).
quotes: The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.

The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every current line of the work order, which is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. A shift on only some lines does not show the prompt.
S4-R5
After successful reassignment, show “Lead technician updated”; after unassigning, show “Lead technician removed”.
Tech plan 1.4 (FF-4 shift scope)
Confirmed: only the outgoing lead's whole-work-order shifts that have not ended

Schedule (top menu) > use the arrows next to Today until the date reads tomorrow > in Search work orders (left) type the number of {Work-order-1} > drag its card onto {Technician-A}'s row and drop it under 8 AM > in the window that opens keep Entire work order selected > use − / + until Hours reads 4h > click Create 1 shift.

doc_part2: Goal: the seven work orders and five shifts of the Preconditions, then drags on Board View with the outcome of each drag recorded.
GET /api/staff lists staff; each row has both id and staff_id, and the Schedule's staffId and the working-hours calls use staff_id.

Create {Customer-A}, its contact and asset, then {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-7} on screen as in Part 1 (two approved lines each). Record each work order's number and id ({Work-order-1 id} … {Work-order-7 id}) and, on {Work-order-3}, {Line-1 id} and {Line-2 id} from the Lines tab requests.

Faster route for shifts, UNVERIFIED on the Work Orders QA site (proven only on the Schedule QA site sv8685, build v3.5-7ec992f): POST /api/schedule/shifts with workOrderId, lineIds (every line id for an entire-work-order shift, the chosen line ids otherwise), staffId, startDate, startTime, spreadMode "single", totalMinutes, perDayMinutes and isAllDay false; 201 means created. If it is refused, use the Schedule screen as in Part 1 and record what the screen sent.

Read shifts back with GET /api/schedule/board?from=<ISO instant>&to=<ISO instant> (full instants such as 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z; a bare date or a range over 62 days is refused). Compare each shift's start and end with the location's time zone before deciding a shift is wrong (SV-11229, a shift saved six hours off, was closed Obsolete on 12 Oct 2026).

Trap: on the Schedule a work order with only one line is booked at once as a whole, with no Entire work order / Choose lines window (recorded in C368178). That is why every work order in this case has two lines.

Run the steps on Board View with Playwright drag-and-drop from the card to the target column. After each drop, wait for either the question (title text starting "Clear ") or the "Lead technician updated" message, and record which appeared; on a question click Keep shifts.

Context: the developer reported on 12 Oct 2026 (SV-11126, build e84b3d1) that the question now opens for an Entire work order shift and not for a shift on only some lines. That is not evidence about the build you test; judge only what you see.
Evidence: a screenshot after each step that has an expected result, the build marker, and the real value of every brace name.

quotes: When changing the lead technician in Board View or Tech View, ask whether to clear the outgoing lead’s work-order-level scheduled shifts.

The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.
If the user chooses to clear shifts, remove only the outgoing lead’s shifts scheduled against that whole work order.
If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.
Never clear shifts scheduled against individual work order lines through this prompt.

The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. doc_part2: Goal: the three work orders and six shifts of the Preconditions, then two drags on Board View and a read of the Schedule.

Create {Customer-A}, its contact and asset, then {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-3} on screen as in Part 1 (two approved lines each). Record {Work-order-1 id}, {Work-order-2 id}, {Work-order-3 id}, {Line-1 id} and {Line-3 id} from the Lines tab requests.

new.title: A line with only a Schedule shift technician follows the new lead technician
preconditions: You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-C} (for example Dana Ortiz) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Technician {Technician-D} (for example Jenny Wilson) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST NT3 Shift Line Follows") is used by this case only.

Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17595) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch"). It has no recorded time and nobody is clocked in to it.
{Line-1} has no technician set through Edit Line; its labor follows the lead {Technician-A}.
{Line-2} has {Technician-C} as its technician, set through Edit Line.
{Technician-B} has a shift tomorrow 9:00–11:00 on {Line-1} only, made on the Schedule.
{Technician-A} has no shift on {Work-order-1}.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
On {Work-order-1}'s card in {Technician-A}'s column, open More actions (…) and click Reassign lead technician.
Choose {Technician-D} and click Reassign.
Click {Work-order-1}'s card to open the work order.
Go to its Lines tab.
Read the Labor row of {Line-1} and of {Line-2}.
Click {Line-1}'s name to open Edit Line.
Read its Technicians.
Close Edit Line without saving.
Click {Line-2}'s name to open Edit Line.
Read its Technicians.
Close Edit Line without saving.
results: Step 4: the lead changes at once with the message "Lead technician updated" and no "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question ({Technician-A} has no shift on this work order); the card moves to {Technician-D}'s column.
Steps 7 and 9: {Line-1} now follows {Technician-D}, and {Technician-B} is still listed among {Line-1}'s technicians.
Steps 7 and 12: {Line-2} still has {Technician-C} as its technician; it did not move to {Technician-D}.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 48 (12 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), the context note under S4-R8 (added in version 46, 12 Oct 2026, after SV-11128), the S4-R8 line table, S4-R5 and S4-R28, read 14 Oct 2026. quotes: S4-R5
After successful reassignment, show “Lead technician updated”; after unassigning, show “Lead technician removed”.

The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every current line of the work order, which is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. A shift on only some lines does not show the prompt.
S4-R8 context note (SV-11128)

"Explicitly assigned" means the line's own technician, set through Edit Line. A technician who is on a line only because of a Schedule shift, whether the shift was dropped on that line or on the entire work order, does not count: the line follows the incoming lead like any other line, and the shift technician stays on the line's technician list.
S4-R8 table: explicit
Explicitly assigned to a different technician | No — the explicit assignment is preserved
